types.name: FMdfAtomicFile
types.doc:
Every document save in both encodings lands here. Writing in place truncates
the target the moment the stream opens, and a bare temp-then-rename is
atomic against a crash but not against lost power, so the write goes through
the PAL's durable replace: the old bytes or the new bytes are the only two
outcomes even across a power cut. The bytes are written verbatim — a
text-mode stream once made a document's line endings depend on the host
that saved it.

headers.doc:
Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.
MDF - Mowo Data Format

Property-level diff and three-way merge of MDF documents (ROADMAP §23.3).

A line diff of a level answers "which lines moved"; an artist asks "which
properties changed". Nodes are matched by (type, name, occurrence among
siblings of that type and name) and properties by key, so a reordered file
diffs empty and two people who changed different properties of one material
merge without a conflict — which a line merge of the same file gets wrong
whenever their edits land on adjacent lines.

Works on any MDF document, packages included: a package's summary is its
first node and diffs like any other. Comments are not part of the diff, but
a merge carries them: each node's and property's comments take whichever
side changed them, and both sides' lines when both did.

headers.doc:
Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.
MDF - Mowo Data Format

Asset packages: one data model, two encodings (ROADMAP §23 D5).

binary — a fixed header, an mdfb summary, an mdfb payload and 16-byte
aligned bulk chunks (geometry, texels, curves) that load on
demand. Meshes, textures, sounds, baked data (.mesh, .tex, ...).
text   — the same summary node followed by the payload nodes, no bulk.
Materials, prefabs, data assets, actor files, levels (.mat,
.prefab, .actor, .mmap, ...).

Every asset type has its own extension (Core/FileTypes.h); the generic
.masset/.mdf an earlier engine wrote are still read.

The SUMMARY is what the asset registry and the content browser read without
loading the asset: class, id, per-subsystem versions, registry tags, the
import table (what the asset references, by id and path, hard or soft) and,
in the binary encoding, the export table and the bulk chunk table.

The payload holds the asset's objects as MDF nodes — Type "Name" { props } —
written by the engine's reflection serializer. The encoding is the type's
choice (bulk data => binary), never the author's; the cook turns everything
binary.

types.name: MdfPackageImport
types.doc:
A reference to another asset. The path survives a rename through the
registry's redirectors; the id is what resolves it.

types.doc: One object the package defines: the payload root of the same index.

types.name: MdfPackageBulk
types.doc:

a reimport compares against) are what the cook strips.

types.name: MdfPackageThumbnail

browser shows it from the registry's read without loading or rendering the

Subsystem -> version of the data it wrote (UE's custom versions): a mesh
loader asks for "mesh", an animation loader for "anim", and each decides
alone what an older version means. Keys are identifiers ([A-Za-z0-9_]):
they are written as property keys.

headers.doc:
Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.
MDF - Mowo Data Format

Parser — parses MDF text format into a Document

Grammar:
document     = node* comment*
node         = comment* IDENTIFIER [STRING] '{' node_body comment* '}'
node_body    = (property | node)*
property     = comment* IDENTIFIER ':' value [comment]   // the trailing one on the same line
value        = STRING | INTEGER | FLOAT | TRUE | FALSE | NULL
| constructor_call | asset_ref | array | enum_value
constructor  = IDENTIFIER '(' arg_list ')'     // vec2, vec3, vec4, quat, rgb, rgba, uuid, hex
asset_ref    = '@' STRING
array        = '[' [value (',' value)*] ']'
enum_value   = IDENTIFIER

Copyright 2025 Mowo Games. All Rights Reserved.
MDF - Mowo Data Format

Writer — serializes MdfDocument to human-readable text format

String escaping contract: the writer escapes '"' '\' '\n' '\r' '\t' with
their shorthand forms, NUL as \0, and every other control character
< 0x20 as \xHH (exactly two hex digits). The lexer decodes all of these,
so any std::string payload round-trips byte-exact through text form.
Bytes >= 0x20 (including UTF-8 sequences) pass through unescaped.

free.name: WriteComments
free.signature: inline void MdfWriter::WriteComments(const std::vector<std::string>& comments, int depth)
free.doc:
Verbatim, one per line at the owner's indent. A block comment keeps its
inner newlines and whatever indentation its continuation lines had, so a
file written at the indent it was read at comes back byte-identical.

free.name: SanitizeIdentifier
free.doc:
Node types and property keys are written RAW — unquoted and unescaped — so
anything that is not an identifier produces a file the parser cannot read
back (a display name with a space cost a whole scene once). Sanitising here
keeps a bad name from destroying the document: the type still round-trips as
an identifier, and the mismatch surfaces as an unknown-type warning on load
rather than a parse failure that takes the file with it.

free.name: WriteNodeInternal
free.signature: inline void MdfWriter::WriteNodeInternal(const MdfNode& node, int depth)

free.name: FormatFloat
free.doc:
Shortest round-trip, at the width the value actually came from. Every
engine float reaches here promoted to double, so 0.35f arrives as
0.34999999403953552 and a fixed eight significant digits wrote it back as
0.34999999 — a number nobody typed, re-quantized on every save. Integer-
valued floats < 1e15 still print as "<int>.0", and ".0" is appended when
the shortest form has neither '.' nor 'e'.
